title: Integration: the trust layer is worth more than its parts
summary: An ablation ladder on the same transfers, a causal day-by-day closed loop, and the Case Linker against simple alert aggregation.

headline.label: Scams paused: Pause Check alone → with Case Linker feedback
Real scam alerts in the top 5 items

sections.title: What each layer adds (whole test window, 597 real scams)
sections.lead: Same transfers, same thresholds; only the layers change.
sections.takeaway: Feeding Case Linker findings back as a watchlist raises scams paused from 82.9% to 92.0% for only 13 extra false pauses (7.8 → 7.9 per 1,000).

sections.title: The closed loop, day by day
sections.lead: Each evening the Case Linker links the day's alerts (only past events); wallets in strong multi-victim cases are watched the next day.
sections.takeaway: 54 extra scams (Tk 153,400) were paused only because the system as a whole remembered the ring.

sections.title: Case Linker vs simple alert aggregation (the same 377 alerts)
sections.lead: Does linking help analysts beyond grouping alerts by the receiving wallet?
sections.takeaway: Simple grouping puts 30% of real scam alerts in the top 5 items and finds no cash-out point; the Case Linker puts 94% there and finds 72% of the cash-outs.

sections.title: QR Shield inside the chain
sections.lead: Scam money that mules cash out through QR payments in the test window (unseen shops).

rows: scam money cashed out via QR
share through shops QR Shield flags

sections.takeaway: Every scam QR cash-out in the test window went through a shop QR Shield had flagged: each is a point where an analyst can intervene.

caveats: The closed loop uses only events before each decision day; ground truth includes unreported scams.
Watchlist rule (chain score ≥ 0.95 and ≥ 2 alerts) is a design choice, not tuned on the test window.
